findings.issue: The dependency graph (state/backlog.md:194) and the summary line (:200) declare CM-C7 an independent root 'startable today with no human and no licence', but the CM-C7 header (:1163) says 'DEPENDS-ON: CM-C1 (merged) and CM-C2a merged (dotnet/CatMetro.Services/ project skeleton)'. Both cannot be true; a reader picking work off the graph starts a blocked contract.
findings.fix: Pick one. Either (a) redraw the graph as CM-C2a -> CM-C7 and drop CM-C7 from 'startable today' (leaving CM-C2a and CM-C4 as the two roots), or (b) give CM-C7 ownership of dotnet/CatMetro.Services/CatMetro.Services.csproj creation, remove it from CM-C2a criterion 2, and make CM-C2a's IContentSource declaration depend on whichever lands first.

findings.issue: Neither contract owns an executable host, and their own code cannot do file I/O. CM-C5 criterion 15 requires 'bash scripts/validate-content.sh' to run a batch validator over content/levels/** and docs/plan/data/stress_boards.json; CM-C6 criterion 6 requires 'scripts/validate-dailies.sh --out <path>'. The ownership table gives CM-C5 and CM-C6 no path under dotnet/**, so there is no project they may make an exe. The only libraries are CM-C2a's (dotnet/CatMetro.Content, dotnet/CatMetro.Services), and changing OutputType or adding a Program.cs there is a diff into a CM-C2a-owned path. Worse, CM-C2a criterion 2 appends a scripts/check.sh block failing on any 'UnityEngine|System\.IO' match under unity/Assets/Scripts/Content/** - which is exactly where CM-C5's Validation/** and CM-C6's Daily/** live - so neither can open a file at all.
findings.fix: Add to the ownership table: CM-C5 owns 'dotnet/CatMetro.Validator/**' (a netstandard-referencing console exe hosting file I/O and an on-disk IContentSource implementation) and CM-C6 owns 'dotnet/CatMetro.DailyTools/**'; both register in dotnet/CatMetro.sln under the existing registration-only exception. Restate CM-C5 criterion 15 and CM-C6 criterion 6 as 'the script invokes dotnet run on the owned host project'. Add a non-goal to both: 'no System.IO under unity/Assets/Scripts/Content/** - all reads go through IContentSource, per CM-C2a criterion 2'.

findings.issue: CM-C2a criterion 4 appends a check.sh block that fails on any *.cs match of 'TypeNameHandling' under unity/Assets/Scripts/** 'except the single settings-construction site'. CM-C7 A-C7-3 requires the save payload to be serialised with TypeNameHandling = None, which is a second construction site under Application/Save/**. The registration exception forbids later contracts from restructuring or altering existing check.sh blocks (state/backlog.md:127-128), so CM-C7 cannot pass CM-C2a's gate without a forbidden edit. Under concurrency this is a hard deadlock, not a merge conflict.
findings.fix: Restate CM-C2a criterion 4 as: 'exactly one JsonSerializerSettings construction site exists, in CatMetro.Content (e.g. ContentJson.Settings), and it sets TypeNameHandling = None; the check.sh block fails on any TypeNameHandling occurrence outside that one file path.' Then add to CM-C7 criterion 2 or 13: 'the save serialiser reuses CatMetro.Content's settings factory (ADR-0003 permits Application -> Content) and constructs no settings object of its own.' Same sentence for CM-C8's queue serialisation.

findings.issue: ADR-0009:33 makes the required `ci` job assert 'config/runtime_bounds.json <-> unity/Assets/StreamingAssets/config/runtime_bounds.json byte-identity'. CM-C7 criterion 12 authors config/runtime_bounds.json but owns no StreamingAssets path (unity/Assets/StreamingAssets/content/** belongs to CM-C2b; .../config/** is unowned by every contract in the queue), and the copy step is mentioned nowhere in the contract. As written, the first contract to author the file lands a repo state the required check will reject once wired, with no owner for the fix.
findings.fix: Either grant CM-C7 'unity/Assets/StreamingAssets/config/**' plus a criterion asserting the two files are byte-identical, or add an explicit non-goal to CM-C7: 'the StreamingAssets copy step (ADR-0009:33, ADR-0008 copy step) is deferred to the content-pipeline contract; the PR records that the ci byte-identity assertion is unsatisfiable until then and names the follow-up.' Silence is the only unacceptable option.

findings.issue: The criterion says the file 'contains exactly the 13 rows of ADR-0006:171-193' and then enumerates 15 keys (schemaVersion plus 14 constants), which is also what ADR-0006 section 4 actually contains. An 'exactly N' assertion whose N contradicts its own enumeration is not independently testable.
findings.fix: Change to 'exactly the 15 keys of ADR-0006 section 4 (schemaVersion + 14 constants)' and keep the enumeration as the authoritative list.

findings.issue: The Q-P row (state/backlog.md:57) states stress boards 'run stages 1-7 and 10'; criterion 14 (:952) states 'Stress boards run stages 1-8 and 10'. Stage 8 (difficulty check) is in one and not the other, and stage 8 is the one whose axis-B basis is UNCONFIGURED (Q-R), so the difference is load-bearing for the exit code.
findings.fix: Pick the criterion's reading (1-8 and 10, since stress boards carry an authored difficultyTarget of 0.30/0.35 that is worth checking) and correct the Q-P row to match; add stage 11 to the SKIPPED set or state explicitly that stress boards do emit a human-playtest checklist row, since stress_boards.json:2 says they need 'plus human playtest'.

findings.issue: The check requires 'one asserting a round-trip LevelGraph -> id lookup returns the original authored ids in order'. The shipped LevelGraph (unity/Assets/Scripts/Domain/LevelGraph.cs:21-44) carries only 'public readonly string LevelId' plus dense integer arrays - there is no node/edge/switch/station id table and no lookup member. As written the criterion cannot be met without adding a member to a frozen Domain type, which is the contract's own stop condition 3.
findings.fix: Re-word: 'the importer returns a CatMetro.Content id map (id -> dense index and index -> id) alongside the LevelGraph; the round-trip assertion runs against that map, not against LevelGraph, which by design carries only LevelId.'

findings.issue: The [CI] grep 'no other source file in unity/Assets/Scripts/Content/** contains a bare integer literal from this list' is unimplementable as stated - the list includes 1, 2, 3, 6, 8, 10, 12, 16, 40, so the grep would fire on ordinary code (array indices, `schemaVersion == 2`). It also scans Content/Validation/** and Content/Daily/**, which CM-C5 and CM-C6 own, so a correct CM-C5 diff can break a CM-C2a criterion.
findings.fix: Restrict the grep to the distinctive values only (262144, 4000, 524288-class multi-digit constants and 70, 40, 30, 12) and scope its root to 'unity/Assets/Scripts/Content/** EXCEPT Validation/** and Daily/**', matching the ownership table's own EXCEPT clauses.

findings.issue: CompletionTicks is defined as 'the tick at which Outcome.Kind became Won'. In the shipped Step, Won is set at Simulation.cs:159-160 and state.Tick is incremented afterwards, so ReplayHasher.RunToEnd returns a state whose Tick is CompletionTicks + 1. Criterion 9's check ('RunToEnd yields Outcome.Kind == Won at CompletionTicks') is therefore off by one as written, and criterion 6's 'hand-computed value for the L001 optimal log' is ambiguous by one tick.
findings.fix: State the identity explicitly: 'CompletionTicks == ReplayHasher.RunToEnd(graph, seed, log).Tick - 1, because Simulation.cs:159-163 sets Won before incrementing Tick'; assert that equation in criterion 9.

findings.issue: Criterion 3 requires DAILY_PREVALIDATION_DAYS to be declared in config/daily_pipeline.json and the criterion instance to run it, and criterion 4 requires SALT_MAX_K in the same file - but stop condition 3 says to stop on 'any temptation to commit a weekday curve, a horizon value or a salt ceiling that is not human-ratified', while A-C6-2 simultaneously authorises the agent to author SALT_MAX_K. The contract both requires and forbids the same commit; criterion 3 cannot pass without Q-Q being resolved, violating the 'no criterion needs a pin resolved' bar.
findings.fix: The horizon is not actually unpinned: PRD CM-R46 ('90 dates pre-validated in CI', docs/prd/PRD.md:727) and ADR-0009:35 ('the next 90 dates') both give 90. Restate criterion 3 as 'DAILY_PREVALIDATION_DAYS = 90, copied from ADR-0009:35 / CM-R46 as a corpus number (the same status as the beam widths); the 30-date run is the smoke instance', and narrow stop condition 3 to the weekday curve only, leaving SALT_MAX_K governed by A-C6-2's declare-with-derivation route.

findings.issue: The check names 'tests/fixtures/content-bad/broken-level.json', a path the ownership table assigns to CM-C2a. CM-C2a's criteria 7 and 8 create fixtures but never that filename, so CM-C5 would have to write into another contract's tree - which the resolution rule makes an out-of-scope diff.
findings.fix: Either move the fixture to a CM-C5-owned path ('tests/validation/fixtures/broken-level.json') or add 'tests/fixtures/content-bad/broken-level.json' to CM-C2a criterion 7's enumerated fixture set and have CM-C5 consume it read-only.

findings.issue: The heading says 'Acceptance criteria (12)' and 13 are listed; the footnote at :387-388 explains the discrepancy by referring to 'the contract header count of 12 in the index table', but the index table carries no criterion counts. A stranger cannot tell how many criteria must pass.
findings.fix: Change the heading to 'Acceptance criteria (13)' and delete the footnote.

findings.issue: The criterion lists 'LevelGraph construction' among the throws pruned per successor. LevelGraph's pin guards fire in its constructor (LevelGraph.cs:64,68), and the graph is a single input built once before the search, so a wild-colour or second-source board never reaches the search at all - there is nothing to prune.
findings.fix: Scope the prune to Simulation.Step and SimOutcome.MakeFailed. Add one sentence: 'A LevelGraph that cannot be constructed never reaches the solver; that failure belongs to CM-C2a criterion 10 / CM-C5 stage 1.'

findings.issue: CM-C2b, CM-C3, CM-C6, CM-C7 and CM-C8 each carry an explicit monetization-tripwire clause naming the AGENTS.md globs and/or the state/mode=production requirement. CM-C2a's non-goals say only 'no save, no ledger, no analytics, no SDK, no commerce'; CM-C4 and CM-C5 have no monetization line in their non-goals and no tripwire stop condition at all.
findings.fix: Add to CM-C4 and CM-C5 non-goals and to CM-C2a's list: 'No path matching **/billing/**, **/iap/** or **/ads/**; any such need is a stop condition requiring state/mode=production first (AGENTS.md Risky paths).' One line each.

findings.issue: The criterion says 'SolverBounds.MAX_NODES_EXPANDED caps total expansions ... declared in one place' and the check says 'one NUnit case with the cap set low'. A const cannot be set low from a test; the criterion does not say how the budget is injected.
findings.fix: Add: 'the search takes an optional expansion budget parameter defaulting to SolverBounds.MAX_NODES_EXPANDED; the test passes a low value.'

findings.issue: product_spec.md:509 defines axis H as 'min(queue+platform slack) during solver trace peak load'. The proxy field is MinQueueSlackAtPeak only - the platform-slack component is silently dropped (reasonably, since platform overflow is pinned out at Outcomes.cs:40), but the omission is not recorded, so CM-C5 stage 8 will compute an H that is not the spec's H without anyone noticing.
findings.fix: Rename the field or add a note: 'axis H's platform-slack term is unreachable while Q-J/NEW-Q4 are open; MinQueueSlackAtPeak is the queue term only, and CM-C5 stage 8 prints H as PARTIAL(Q-J).'

findings.issue: Both drive the PlatformOverflow case from 'a constructed presentation-level outcome' because SimOutcome.MakeFailed throws (Outcomes.cs:40-42). Nothing in the contract prevents that construct from becoming a shipped parallel outcome type that carries PlatformOverflow through Presentation - which is exactly the semantics the pin exists to keep out of the tree.
findings.fix: Add to criterion 1: 'the constructed outcome type is test-only and lives under unity/Assets/Tests/**; a [CI] grep asserts no type under Presentation/** or Application/** constructs a FailReason.PlatformOverflow value.'

findings.issue: (a) The summary-line assertion is written as the regex '^test: ([0-9]+)/\1 passed'; \1 is a backreference, which POSIX ERE (grep -E) does not support, so the named check is not runnable as written on the default toolchain. (b) The dependency ASCII at state/backlog.md:190 places '(DEPENDS-ON CM-C2a + CM-C4)' on the CM-C4 line, reading as though CM-C4 depends on itself; it belongs on the CM-C5 line.
findings.fix: (a) Specify grep -P, or assert the simpler invariant that scripts/test.sh exits 0 and stdout matches '^test: [0-9]+/[0-9]+ passed' with the two numbers equal, checked in the wrapper. (b) Move the annotation one line down.
